newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Fincantieri sees interim and 96 profit up.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Fincantieri sees interim and 96 profit up.

text.p: Italian state shipbuilder Fincantieri posted a 54 percent rise in net profit in the first half of this year and sees full 1996 profit jumping 60 percent on last year, senior company officials said.
Fincantieri recorded a 12.5 billion profit in the first six months against 8.1 billion in the same 1995 period, the officials said confirming press reports.
For the whole of 1996, the shipbuilder expects to post net profit of 40 billion lire against a 25 billion lire 1995 profit.

Fincantieri, part of state industrial holding IRI, said the improved interim result was mainly due to a rigorous cost-cutting policy linked to the company's strength in the cruise liner sector where the group said it has 47 percent market share in terms of gross tonnage.
On October 19, Fincantieri delivered to Carnival Corp the largest cruise ship in the world, the $400 million, 101,000 gross ton "Carnival Destiny'.
Its current cruise ship orderbook contains nine vessels worth a total 5.5 trillion lire under construction for P&O Cruises, Carnival Cruise Line, Holland America Line and Disney Cruises.
On October 31, Fincantieri laid the keel at its Venice Marghera yard of the cruise ship "Disney Magic', the first of two 85,000 gross ton sister ships for the Walt Disney Co.
The second ship, the "Disney Wonder', will also be built at Marghera. The two new vessels will be launched at the beginning and at the end of 1998 respectively.
Cruise industry experts estimate that Disney spent more than $300 million to build each ship.
